units.title: A workshop that changed its plan
units.text:
Our neighbourhood group has organised repair workshops for the past three months. At first, we invited everyone to bring broken household objects on the same Saturday morning. The room became crowded, and several visitors left before anyone could help them. We received positive comments about the volunteers, but complaints about the long wait.

For next month, we have decided to offer two shorter sessions. People who need help with bicycles should book the early session; the later one will focus on small electrical items. Both sessions will remain free. Volunteers have also asked visitors to describe the problem when booking, so they can prepare suitable tools. We cannot promise that every object will be repaired, but we hope fewer people will leave without receiving advice.

units.title: A library tries a new schedule
units.text:
The town library usually closes at six, but many people who work during the day have asked for later opening hours. The library cannot afford to keep every room open in the evening, so it will test a smaller service on Thursdays for six weeks. Visitors will be able to collect reserved books and use the reading area until eight. The computer room will still close at six.

If enough people use the evening service, the library will consider continuing it after the trial. Staff will count visits and collect short comments, but a decision has not been made. Some visitors have already asked whether the library will open later on other weekdays. The manager says the first priority is to find out whether Thursday evenings are useful before making a wider promise.

units.title: Computers for another school
units.text:
At the end of the school year, twelve computers were collected from a local office. They still worked, but they were too slow for some of the office's new programs. A volunteer team checked the machines and replaced parts where necessary. The computers were then prepared for a nearby school that needed equipment for basic writing and research tasks.

Before delivery, the office asked a technician to remove its private files. The volunteers explained that the machines would not be suitable for demanding design software, even after repairs. The school accepted this limitation because its immediate need was to give more pupils access to simple digital lessons. A teacher said the donation would be useful, but added that the school still needed enough time and staff to introduce the computers into classes.

units.title: A reading partner who listens
units.text:
When I joined the language exchange group, I hoped to improve my speaking, but I often stayed quiet. I could understand short articles, yet I became nervous when someone asked me to explain my opinion. The group leader introduced me to Clara, a student who had joined a year earlier and remembered having the same problem.

Clara suggested that we read a short news story before each meeting and each prepare two questions. During our first sessions, she let me finish my answers before giving feedback. She also asked me to explain why I agreed or disagreed with the writer, rather than repeat sentences from the article. I still make mistakes, and I sometimes need extra time, but now I speak more often. I have learned that preparing ideas is useful, while listening patiently can make practice less frightening.

units.title: The lights during the meeting
units.text:
Last Wednesday, the residents of our building were discussing the new corridor lights when the electricity went off for a few minutes. Some people wondered whether the new system had caused the problem. However, a technician later explained that several buildings on the street had lost power at the same time. The residents agreed that this information did not support blaming the new lights.

The meeting continued after the power returned. A few neighbours said they liked the lights turning on automatically when someone entered, while others wanted clearer signs showing how to report a fault. The building manager promised to place instructions near the lifts and to record any complaints during the next month. Nobody presented figures showing how much energy the system had saved, so the group decided not to make a public claim about savings yet.
